issues.title: Keyspace USE failures are never classed transient vs permanent, pool can stay Broken…
issues.verdictReason: handle_ready_connection's new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) arm (connection_pool.rs:900-911) unconditionally drops the connection, sets had_error_since_last_refill, and if the pool is empty publishes Broken(err). Every scheduled refill (backoff capped by refill_delay_strategy) reopens connections only to fail USE and discard them the same way, so a persistent keyspace failure (dropped keyspace, permission revoked) leaves the whole node's pool permanently Broken and endlessly churns open-then-discard connection attempts; pre-PR code instead silently kept the misconfigured connection (worse for correctness but didn't take the whole node down).
issues.scopeReason: The Keyspace error arm and its unconditional drop-and-mark-broken behavior were added by commit 7f48315d in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: A keyspace that stays unusable drains every node pool for good; endless open-then-discard churn while USE keeps failing (backoff capped at 10s).

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: The new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace) branch drops the connection on any UseKeyspaceError including permanent ones, current_keyspace is never rolled back, and every refill fails the same way, opening then discarding connections, ending with the pool published as Broken(UseKeyspaceError).

issues.title: Keyspace-error branch skips the staleness check the success branch performs on…
issues.verdictReason: The Ok() branch (connection_pool.rs:915-917) compares evt.keyspace_name against the live self.current_keyspace before accepting a connection, but the Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) branch above it has no equivalent check; a USE for a keyspace that was requested before a later use_keyspace() call changed current_keyspace is still treated as a current failure, which can wrongly flag had_error_since_last_refill and publish Broken with a stale keyspace's error even though the session has already moved on to a different, possibly-working keyspace.
issues.scopeReason: This asymmetry exists only because the PR split the old single Ok(..) handling into separate Keyspace/Connection error arms without carrying the staleness check into the new error arm.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: A USE failure for an outdated keyspace still drops the connection instead of retrying with the new keyspace.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: The Keyspace error branch never compares evt.keyspace_name with self.current_keyspace although the success branch does, so a USE for keyspace A that fails after the session switched to keyspace B is dropped instead of retried with B, and the pool may be published Broken with an error about the old keyspace.

issues.title: USE-keyspace failure log downgraded from warn! to debug!, hiding it at default log level
issues.verdictReason: The pre-PR start_setting_keyspace_for_connection logged USE failures with warn!; the diff removes that and the new handle_ready_connection Keyspace-error arm logs the same event with debug! (connection_pool.rs:903), while remove_connection's keyspace-unrelated error path elsewhere in the file still uses warn!, so this specific regression in visibility is real and was introduced by this PR.
issues.scopeReason: The log level change is part of the same commit (7f48315d) that introduced the new error-handling branch.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Failure log was lowered from warn! to debug!, making USE failures invisible at default log levels.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: The failure log was lowered from warn! to debug! in the same change that made the failure drop connections, so a pool that stays under its target size because of USE failures is now invisible at default log levels, while a related keyspace failure elsewhere in the same file still logs at warn!.

issues.title: Commit 0d91aa54 fails a no-default-features -D warnings build (unused FutureExt import)
issues.verdictReason: Checked out commit 0d91aa54 in a worktree and ran `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check -p scylla --tests --no-default-features`: it fails with `error: unused import: futures::FutureExt` at connection_pool.rs:1445 (that commit's line), because at that point FutureExt is only used inside a #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] test. The same command succeeds cleanly at HEAD (617139df), since 7f48315d adds a non-cfg-gated now_or_never() use. CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly requires 'Every commit in your patch compiles, passes static checks ... and passes all tests.'
issues.scopeReason: The broken intermediate commit is part of this PR's own commit sequence and violates the repo's documented per-commit build requirement.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Commit 0d91aa54 does not build on its own under -Dwarnings without the metrics feature.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: The futures::FutureExt import is not behind a feature guard, but in commit 0d91aa54 its only use is inside a #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] test, which CI's no-features -Dwarnings check fails on; it only becomes used in 7f48315d (now_or_never).

issues.title: Excess shard-aware connection retried via non-shard-aware port leaks a total_connections…
issues.verdictReason: When a shard-aware connection lands on an already-full shard, the `else if evt.requested_shard.is_some()` arm (connection_pool.rs:994-1006) just drops `connection` and calls start_opening_connection(None) without calling decrement_total_connections, even though inc_total_connections was already counted for it in start_opening_connection's count_in_metrics closure; this is unchanged by the diff (pure context in the PR) and predates the PR's metrics-balancing commits, which added decrements at other sites (:674, :1031, :1114) but not here.
issues.scopeReason: This branch is untouched context in the diff; the leak predates the PR and the PR's metrics-balancing work did not touch or make this path newly reachable.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: A shard-aware connection landing on a full shard is dropped without decrementing total_connections.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: A shard-aware connection that lands on a full shard is dropped without decrementing total_connections; this leak already existed on the base branch and is outside what the PR changed, but the PR's metrics-balancing commits leave this removal path unbalanced.

issues.title: Resharding's excess-connections term in decrement_total_connections is untested
issues.verdictReason: maybe_reshard's decrement_total_connections(active_connection_count() + excess_connections.len()) at connection_pool.rs:1114-1116 was added by this PR. issues.title: Public #[from] UseKeyspaceError conversion on ConnectionError called unneeded API surface
issues.verdictReason: Every other error-wrapping variant already on ConnectionError (BrokenConnection, ConnectionSetupRequestError, TranslationError, etc.) uses the same #[from] pattern, and the new UseKeyspaceError variant is actively used via `err.into()` in handle_ready_connection; using #[from] here is consistent with the enum's existing convention, not an unnecessary deviation.
issues.scopeReason: The variant and its #[from] attribute were added by this PR, so any design question about it is this PR's to own even though the verdict is false-positive.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Public #[from] UseKeyspaceError conversion on ConnectionError is unneeded API surface.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-baseline-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: The public #[from] UseKeyspaceError conversion on ConnectionError was raised as unneeded API surface.

issues.verdictReason: The PR's Validation section lists only a focused test run, a default-feature `cargo check`, `cargo fmt --check` and `git diff --check` - no clippy and no metrics feature. .github/workflows/rust.yml runs `cargo clippy --all-features` and `cargo check --all-targets -p scylla --all-features` in CI.
